I have several promising sources.

For VLA on-device inference:
- `https://arxiv.org/html/2602.18397v1` ("How Fast Can I Run My VLA?") seems very technical and likely to discuss latency and bottlenecks.
- `https://medium.com/openvino-toolkit/deploy-production-grade-physical-ai-with-reduced-complexity-b5451d68221c` and `https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/tools/openvino-toolkit/physical-ai.html` discuss hardware acceleration (OpenVINO).
- `https://blog.pebblous.ai/project/PhysicalAI/physical-ai/en/` mentions edge AI inference as a bottleneck.

For Humanoid Actuator Energy Efficiency:
- `https://roboticsandautomationnews.com/2026/03/12/challenges-in-bipedal-locomotion-dexterous-manipulation-and-power-efficiency/99584/`
- `https://www.xrobotek.com/news/optimizing-energy-efficiency-in-humanoid-robot-actuators.html`
- `https://hub.stabilarity.com/thermal-management-heat-dissipation-actuator-cooling-and-operating-temperature-envelopes-for-humanoid-robots/` (Thermal management is closely linked to energy efficiency).
- `https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/smb2.12008` (Comprehensive review).

I will start by reading the Arxiv paper on VLA inference and the Intel/OpenVINO pages for hardware acceleration. Then I'll move to the actuator energy efficiency sources.
